items.plain: We cherish those who love us, and time with them makes up for much misery. But those who reject us as unworthy matter even more: they show us a higher life and stir new powers to attempt new things.
items.core_idea: Those who reject us push us to grow

items.plain: We are frozen by fear, clinging to house, land, job and money because they have fed us, though we admit our real life does not flow through them. We long to be set on fire and made useful.
items.core_idea: Fear makes us cling to possessions instead of greatness

items.plain: The best people believe that, in sum, one person is worth about the same as another. Each excels in something, and each weakness is compensated, since every limitation concentrates a person's strength.
items.core_idea: Every weakness concentrates strength somewhere else

items.plain: Once you see that a higher will governs everything without exception, you grow calm. The earth carries us safely without our help; our own path is our only job, and we needn't manage the universe.
items.core_idea: Tend your own orbit; the universe runs itself

items.plain: Don't rush to expose the false reputations of prominent people. They are working harder at revealing themselves and will succeed. Hold back your criticism for a few days, and their inadequacy will be plain to everyone.
items.core_idea: Pretenders expose themselves without your help

items.plain: Living amid wonder, we owe cheer, courage and aspiration. The wise marvel at the ordinary. Having received so much, the heart can trust the Power and the Soul that guide it, sure the future will match the past.
items.core_idea: Wonder at the ordinary and trust the guiding Soul

items.plain: Everywhere we are close to the best. We put off our hopes, and that delay is the root of idleness and crime; while waiting, we kill time with jokes, sleep, eating and wrongdoing.
items.core_idea: Deferring our hopes breeds idleness and wrongdoing

items.plain: A person who prizes his own talent finds, out in the wider world, that others have different gifts and he is useless in their places. Every gift gets its turn, and we all take turns at the top.
items.core_idea: Every talent has its turn; we all rotate

items.plain: If one person were perfect, there would be no need for the rest of us. As long as anyone exists, he is needed for something, so let him stand up for his own part.
items.core_idea: Everyone alive is needed for something

items.plain: When you criticise a great mind, you are probably attacking your own caricature of it. Every person has something infinite in them, a channel of heaven, so criticising them can amount to cutting off your own soul.
items.core_idea: Criticising others often wounds your own soul

items.plain: The world's secret is that nothing truly dies; things only step out of sight for a while and then come back.
items.core_idea: Nothing dies; things withdraw and return

items.plain: Love reveals nature's riches by showing hidden worth in a friend, suggesting equal good everywhere. As a good fruit costs no more effort than a poor one, I want only the best in work, speech, thought and friends.
items.core_idea: Love reveals hidden worth; settle only for the best

items.plain: If only we were safe from moods! Even sincere teachers soon disown what they passionately preached, and we keep shifting our viewpoint. Knowing there are always other moods, I am never wholly sincere.
items.core_idea: Shifting moods make every conviction unstable

items.plain: We can speak frankly and fully yet leave feeling nothing was said, because people cannot truly know each other. When a companion assumes he knows my mind, endless explanation leaves us exactly where we began.
items.core_idea: Assuming we understand each other blocks real understanding

items.plain: The daydreams of sincere people foretell the future. What a sensitive young person privately imagines but fears to say becomes public resolutions, then a cause fought over, then established law for a century, until new dreams replace it.
items.core_idea: Today's private dreams become tomorrow's laws

items.plain: While I govern myself, my neighbour and I can often work together. But when I try to direct him too, I overstep and the relationship becomes false; even if he cannot protest, it is a lie that hurts us both.
items.core_idea: Controlling others creates false, harmful relationships

items.plain: If I put myself in my child's place and we see things together, that shared understanding guides us both. But if I guess at his situation from outside and give orders, he will never obey me.
items.core_idea: Shared understanding guides; outside orders fail

items.plain: Knowing we fall short of the great character we owe, we show off some small talent as a substitute. It may impress others, but it doesn't calm us or give us real strength; we carry a quiet penance.
items.core_idea: Showing off talent cannot replace real character

items.plain: No one would choose to be a fraud if they could afford to be honest.
items.core_idea: People fake it only when honesty feels unaffordable

items.plain: Every person has a right to work, to be trusted, loved and honoured. A state founded on the power of love has never yet been attempted.
items.core_idea: A state built on love has never been tried

items.plain: Time arrives feeling open and sacred, then gets chopped into trivial chores, errands, headaches, taxes, tiresome dealings and the sting of awkward words. Whatever we do, life brings its petty annoyances, like flies in summer.
items.core_idea: Petty chores and annoyances eat up our time

items.plain: Every simple, innocent act yields some wisdom. A homebody who loves the ticking clock and the crackle of logs on the fire has comforts others never imagine.
items.core_idea: Simple domestic life holds quiet wisdom and comfort

items.plain: If you keep a law, any law, your path will be full of satisfactions. Pleasures differ more in quality than in quantity.
items.core_idea: Living by a law brings satisfaction

items.plain: To be good, words and actions must come at the right time. Sharpening a scythe sounds cheerful in June, but the same sound is lonely and sad when it is too late to make hay.
items.core_idea: Good words and deeds must be timely

items.plain: Every lie harms the liar and the health of society; even a profitable lie is later heavily taxed by events. Frankness invites frankness. Trust people and they will be true to you; treat them greatly and they will show greatness.
items.core_idea: Honesty and trust bring out the best in others

items.plain: Anyone who wants peace of mind must steel his resolve. Face the thing you fear most, and your firmness will usually show the fear was groundless. As the Latin proverb says, the eye is beaten first in battle.
items.core_idea: Face your worst fear and it shrinks

items.plain: In quarrels with neighbours, fear exaggerates the other side, and it gives bad advice. Everyone feels weak inside and looks strong to others. You fear him, and he fears you; up close, bullies are timid.
items.core_idea: Those you fear are just as afraid of you

items.plain: Love is said to be blind, but kindness actually helps us see. When you meet an opponent, ignore the dividing lines and meet on whatever common ground remains; it will widen fast until the barriers dissolve.
items.core_idea: Meet opponents on common ground and barriers melt

items.plain: We hold back from closeness with the people around us, as if waiting for something better. But tomorrow will be like today, and life slips away while we prepare to live. Let us enjoy the affections near us.
items.core_idea: Life wastes while we wait; cherish nearby affections

items.plain: A person is his own guiding star; an honest, complete soul commands all light and fate, and nothing comes to him too early or too late. Our deeds, good or bad, are our angels and shadows that stay with us.
items.core_idea: Our own acts shape our fate

items.plain: Watch the flashes of insight in your own mind more than famous poets and sages. We dismiss our thoughts because they're ours, then meet them in great works. Hold to your own impressions, or a stranger will voice them first.
items.core_idea: Trust your own insights before others voice them

items.plain: In time everyone learns that envy is ignorance and imitation is suicide; you must accept yourself as you are, and good comes only through work on your own plot. Your power is new, and you only discover it by trying.
items.core_idea: Accept yourself; your power is found by trying

items.plain: We only half express ourselves, ashamed of the divine idea each of us embodies, but God won't have his work shown by cowards. You feel relieved and glad after putting your heart into your work; anything less gives no peace.
items.core_idea: Wholehearted effort brings peace; half-effort does not

items.plain: Trust yourself; every heart responds to that. Accept the place, people and times divine providence has given you, as great men did, trusting what works within them. We must take up that destiny boldly, not as cowards hiding.
items.core_idea: Trust yourself and accept your providential place

items.plain: Society everywhere conspires against the independence of its members. It is like a company where people trade their freedom for security. Its favourite virtue is conformity; it hates self-reliance and prefers names and customs to real creators.
items.core_idea: Society demands conformity and resists self-reliance

items.plain: To be truly a person you must be a nonconformist and test whether what is called good really is. Nothing is finally sacred except the integrity of your own mind. Clear yourself with yourself, and the world will agree.
items.core_idea: Nothing is sacred but your mind's integrity

items.plain: I'm ashamed of how easily we give in to titles, big organisations and dead institutions. Any polite, well-spoken person sways me more than they should. I ought to stand upright and speak the plain truth in every way.
items.core_idea: Stop deferring to titles; speak plain truth

items.plain: Goodness needs some sharpness to it; otherwise it isn't goodness at all.
items.core_idea: Real goodness has an edge

items.plain: I want to live, not to atone or put on a show. I'd rather my life be modest and genuine than dazzling and unsteady. However small my gifts, I exist and need no outside proof of my worth.
items.core_idea: Live genuinely, not for show or approval

items.plain: Only what I must do concerns me, not what people think. It's hard because others always think they know your duty better. The great person keeps, sweetly, the independence of solitude while in the middle of the crowd.
items.core_idea: Keep your independence even amid the crowd

items.plain: Keeping up customs that mean nothing to you scatters your strength, wastes time and blurs who you are. Behind such screens I can't see the real you. Do your own work and I'll know you, and you'll strengthen yourself.
items.core_idea: Dead conformity scatters you; your own work reveals you

items.plain: One humiliating experience is the forced smile we wear among people we're uneasy with, answering talk that bores us. The face muscles, moved not naturally but by a cheap act of will, tighten unpleasantly.
items.core_idea: Forced smiles in company feel false and painful

items.plain: The world punishes nonconformity with disapproval, so you must judge a sour face rightly. The crowd's frowns, like its smiles, have no deep cause; they come and go with the wind and the newspapers.
items.core_idea: The crowd's disapproval is shallow and passing

items.plain: Another fear that stops self-trust is wanting to stay consistent with past words so others aren't disappointed. Why drag that corpse of memory around? If you contradict yourself, so what? Live in a new day.
items.core_idea: Don't let past words chain your present self

items.plain: Foolish consistency is a bugbear of small minds; a great soul ignores it. Say plainly what you think today, and tomorrow say what you think then, even if it contradicts today. Being misunderstood is the lot of the great.
items.core_idea: To be great is to be misunderstood

items.plain: People see us as we truly are. Character speaks louder than our intentions. We think our virtues or vices show only in deeds, but they give off a breath every moment.
items.core_idea: Character shows constantly, not only in actions

items.plain: Even the best ship sails a zigzag course, yet from far enough away the line looks straight. Your genuine actions will explain one another; conformity explains nothing. Act sincerely, and your past sincere acts will back you up.
items.core_idea: Genuine actions add up to a straight course

items.plain: If I can do right today and ignore who's watching, it's because past right actions now support me. Whatever happens, do right now. Character builds up over time; all the good days before add their strength to this one.
items.core_idea: Character is cumulative; do right now

items.plain: Let us stop bowing and apologising. When an important man comes to dinner, I don't want to please him; I want him to want to please me. I'll stand for humanity, kindly if I can, but truthfully.
items.core_idea: Stop apologising; stand kind but true

items.plain: So a person should know his worth and keep things in their place. He shouldn't sneak around like an outsider or an unwanted guest in a world that exists for him.
items.core_idea: Know your worth; you belong here

items.plain: Kings and lords sound grander than ordinary people doing a day's work, but the substance of life is the same for both. Why revere famous rulers so much? Your private act today carries stakes as great as theirs.
items.core_idea: Ordinary acts matter as much as famous deeds

items.plain: If we live truly, we will see truly. Being strong comes as naturally to the strong as weakness does to the weak.
items.core_idea: Living truly brings true sight

items.plain: A soul lifted above passion sees the oneness and eternal cause of things, sees that Truth and Right exist in themselves, and grows calm knowing all things go well.
items.core_idea: Rising above passion brings calm trust

items.plain: Only living counts, not having lived. Power stops the moment we rest; it exists in the moment of moving from an old state to a new one, in leaping the gap, in darting at a goal.
items.core_idea: Power lives in transition, not rest

items.plain: Why take on the faults of friend, spouse, parent or child just because they share my home or blood? All people share my blood. That's no reason to adopt their bad temper or folly, or feel ashamed of it.
items.core_idea: Family ties don't oblige you to share faults

items.plain: Sometimes the whole world seems to pester you with urgent trifles: friends, clients, children, illness, fear, need all knock at once. Keep your composure and don't enter their confusion. Others can annoy me only through my own weak curiosity.
items.core_idea: Others disturb you only as you allow

items.plain: I appeal against your customs: I must be myself and can't keep breaking myself for others. If you can love me as I am, we'll be happier; if not, I'll still try to deserve it. I won't hide my tastes.
items.core_idea: Be yourself and let others love you as you are

items.plain: Our strength and courage seem drained away, and we have become timid, gloomy whiners. We fear truth, fortune, death and each other.
items.core_idea: We have become timid and afraid of everything

items.plain: Young people lose heart at their first failure. But a sturdy youth who tries trade after trade and always lands on his feet is worth a hundred pampered ones. He doesn't postpone life; he has a hundred chances, not one.
items.core_idea: Don't postpone life; failure leaves a hundred chances

items.plain: Prayer that asks for a particular thing, anything less than all good, is corrupt. True prayer is viewing life's facts from the highest point of view, the joyful speech of a seeing soul, God's spirit declaring his works good.
items.core_idea: True prayer contemplates, it doesn't beg

items.plain: Discontent is a lack of self-reliance, a weakness of will. Grieve over disasters only if it helps the sufferer; otherwise get on with your own work, and the damage already begins to be repaired.
items.core_idea: Discontent is weak will; do your own work

items.plain: Travel is a fool's paradise. I imagine Naples or Rome will dazzle me and lift my sadness, but when I wake up there, the same sad self I fled is beside me. My giant goes with me wherever I go.
items.core_idea: You cannot travel away from yourself

items.plain: Insist on being yourself and never imitate. Your own gift carries a lifetime's development; a borrowed talent you only half own. What each person does best, only their Maker can teach them.
items.core_idea: Develop your own gift; never imitate

items.plain: The Caliph Ali said your share in life is already looking for you, so you can stop chasing after it and be at rest.
items.core_idea: Your lot is seeking you; rest

items.plain: Whoever sees that power is inborn, and that he was weak only from seeking good outside himself, and then trusts his own thought, instantly stands upright and works wonders, like a man on his feet rather than his head.
items.core_idea: Power is within; stop seeking it outside

items.plain: Good news, like a political win, more income, a sick person's recovery or a friend's return, lifts your spirits and you think good days are coming. Don't believe it. Only you, and the triumph of principles, can bring you peace.
items.core_idea: Nothing brings you peace but yourself

items.plain: When we reflect on our lives, we find them wrapped in beauty. Looking back, everything takes on a pleasing shape, like distant clouds; even tragic and dreadful things, and ordinary neglected ones, gain grace in memory.
items.core_idea: In memory, even hard things become beautiful

items.plain: Every loss and pain is particular; to the heart the universe stays unharmed. Troubles and disasters don't lessen our trust. No one has ever described his griefs as lightly as he could have.
items.core_idea: Pain is particular; the whole remains unhurt

items.plain: Nature doesn't want us to fret and fume. She cares little more for our good works and learning than for our frauds and wars. When we leave our busy meetings for the woods, she says, "So worked up, little sir?"
items.core_idea: Nature gently mocks our frantic busyness

items.plain: Everything teaches us faith; we need only obey. There is guidance for each of us, and by listening humbly we will hear the right word. Why agonise over choices? There is a right place and fitting work for you.
items.core_idea: Listen humbly; guidance and your place exist

items.plain: Everyone has a calling, and talent is the call. There is one direction open to each person, where obstacles fall away, like a ship in a river that finds its channel and sweeps calmly out to an endless sea.
items.core_idea: Your talent is your calling

items.plain: What a person does is what he truly has; why hope or fear? His strength is within. He should count as solid only the good that grows from his nature; fortune's gifts come and go like summer leaves.
items.core_idea: Only inner good is solid; fortune passes

items.plain: Certain small memories of people and events stay with you far beyond their apparent importance. They relate to your gift, so give them weight instead of reaching for more usual examples. What your heart thinks great is great.
items.core_idea: What your heart finds great is great

items.plain: No one can learn what they aren't ready for, however close it is. God shields us from ideas that come too early. We can't see what's before us until the mind ripens; then the old blindness seems a dream.
items.core_idea: We learn only when we're ready

items.plain: In the Alps a traveller may see his own shadow swollen into a frightening giant. An old man told his sons, frightened by a shape in the dark, that they would never see anything worse than themselves.
items.core_idea: What frightens us is often our own shadow

items.plain: We wrongly think we must win friends by conforming to society's dress, manners and values. My only true friend is the soul I meet on my own path, neither of us bowing to the other, who shares my experience.
items.core_idea: True friends are met on your own path

items.plain: A person gets the standing he claims. Take the place that is yours and everyone goes along. The world lets each of us set our own value, hero or fool, and accepts whatever measure we take of ourselves.
items.core_idea: The world accepts the value you set on yourself

items.plain: Michelangelo told a young sculptor not to worry much about the lighting on his statue; the light of the public square would show its worth.
items.core_idea: Real worth is tested in the open

items.plain: A person is taken for what he is worth. It's pointless to wonder what others think of us, and just as pointless to fear staying unknown.
items.core_idea: Don't worry about others' opinion or obscurity

items.plain: No sincere word is ever completely lost. No generous act falls to the ground without some heart unexpectedly welcoming it.
items.core_idea: Sincere words and generosity always find a home

items.plain: When you visit a friend, don't waste it apologising for not coming sooner; just visit, letting the highest love reach him through you. Don't torment yourself over gifts not given. Be a gift yourself, shining with real light.
items.core_idea: Skip apologies; be a gift yourself

items.plain: Real action happens in quiet moments. Life's turning points aren't career, marriage or office, but a silent thought on a walk that revises how we live: you did this, but that would be better. Later years serve that thought.
items.core_idea: Life's turning points are quiet thoughts

items.plain: Why belittle who we are out of false modesty? A good person is content. I admire a great hero but don't wish to be him; being told he acted while I sit still won't trouble me. Both are good.
items.core_idea: Be content with who you are

items.plain: Let us find peace by being faithful to our duties. Why wander into history before answering my benefactors, or read of great campaigns before replying to my own letters? Much reading is a timid escape from our work.
items.core_idea: Do your own duties before gazing elsewhere

items.plain: Some hours of life carry more weight and lasting effect than others. Our faith comes in moments, while our faults are habits. Yet those brief moments have a depth that makes them feel more real than everything else.
items.core_idea: Brief moments of faith outweigh habitual faults

items.plain: A person is a stream with a hidden source; our being flows into us from somewhere unknown. No one can foresee the next moment. Every moment I must admit events come from something higher than my own will.
items.core_idea: Our lives flow from a source beyond our will

items.plain: We live in sequences, divisions and fragments. Yet within each person is the soul of the whole: the wise silence, the universal beauty to which every part is equally related, the eternal One.
items.core_idea: Within us lives the soul of the whole

items.plain: A light shines through us onto things and shows us we are nothing, the light is everything. A person is the front of a temple in which all wisdom and goodness live.
items.core_idea: A light within us is everything

items.plain: Our true youth and age aren't measured from birth. Some thoughts, like love of eternal beauty, always find us young and keep us so. In sickness or weariness, a line of poetry or a deep sentence refreshes us beyond time.
items.core_idea: Great thoughts keep us young beyond time

items.plain: We know better than we act. We don't yet fully own ourselves, yet we know we are much more than we seem.
items.core_idea: We are more than we yet live

items.plain: With my child, learning and money are useless; only soul counts. If I'm wilful, he resists and I win only by force. If the soul judges between us, the same soul looks from his eyes, and he loves with me.
items.core_idea: Lead a child by soul, not will

items.plain: We are wiser than we know. If we don't interfere with our thinking and see how things stand in God, we know each thing and every person, because the Maker of all stands behind us and sees through us.
items.core_idea: We are wiser than we know

items.plain: Don't demand a description of the lands you're sailing to. A description can't really show them; tomorrow you'll arrive and know them by living there.
items.core_idea: You'll know the future by living it

items.plain: Our hungry questions about the future betray a fault; God gives them no answer. Our nature veils tomorrow so we learn to live today. Drop idle curiosity, work and live, and the growing soul makes question and answer one.
items.core_idea: The future is veiled so we live today

items.plain: We teach what we are, without meaning to. Thoughts enter and leave our minds by paths we never deliberately opened. Character teaches over our heads.
items.core_idea: We teach what we are, involuntarily

items.plain: Deal so plainly with people that they must be completely sincere with you and can't hope to trifle with you. That is the highest compliment you can give.
items.core_idea: Plain dealing is the highest compliment

items.plain: How dear and soothing the thought of God is to us, filling lonely places and wiping away the scars of our mistakes and disappointments.
items.core_idea: The thought of God comforts and heals

items.plain: What is truly yours comes to you. Seeking a friend, let your feet run, not your mind. If you miss him, accept it's for the best; the power in you is in him too, and would unite you if right.
items.core_idea: What is truly yours will come to you

items.plain: Believe that every word in the world you should hear will reach you. Every proverb or book meant to help or comfort you will find its way home, and every friend your tender heart truly longs for will embrace you.
items.core_idea: What you truly need will find you

items.plain: Faith that rests on authority isn't faith. Leaning on authority shows how far religion has declined and the soul has withdrawn.
items.core_idea: Faith based on authority is not faith

items.plain: Everyone lives by truth and needs to express it. In love, art, greed, politics, work and play, we try to voice our painful secret. A person is only half himself; the other half is his expression.
items.core_idea: We are only half ourselves without expression

items.plain: However often deceived, a person still waits for a companion who can hold him steady to a truth until he has made it his own.
items.core_idea: We long for someone to steady us in truth

items.plain: Even the plainest life gives enough experience to express any thought. Why crave new facts? Day and night, home and garden, a few books and actions serve as well as every trade and spectacle.
items.core_idea: Ordinary experience is rich enough

items.plain: A lost traveller drops the reins and trusts his horse's instinct to find the road; we should do the same with the divine instinct that carries us through this world.
items.core_idea: Trust the divine instinct that carries you

items.plain: You can never cheat nature with a trick. The Creator's calm presence doesn't answer to opium or wine; the great vision comes to a pure, simple soul in a clean body. Drug-made excitement is counterfeit, not inspiration.
items.core_idea: True inspiration comes to the pure, not intoxicated

items.plain: The spirit that satisfies quiet hearts, rising from dry grass and stones in the March sun, comes to the poor and simple. Fill your head with city fashion, greed and stimulants, and you'll find no wisdom in the lonely woods.
items.core_idea: Wisdom comes to quiet, simple hearts

items.plain: Like a lost shepherd dying in snow a few feet from his door, we are dying beside the waters of life and truth. We can't reach any thought but our present one; every thought, every heaven, is a prison.
items.core_idea: We perish within reach of truth

items.plain: Poet, don't doubt; persist. Say: it's in me and it will come out. Stand there, stuck and stammering, jeered at, and keep striving until that dream-power you glimpse each night breaks out, a power beyond all limits.
items.core_idea: Persist until what is in you comes out

items.plain: Wherever snow falls, water flows, birds fly, twilight comes, clouds or stars fill the sky, wherever there is danger, awe and love, there is Beauty, plentiful as rain, poured out for you. No place on earth is unfit for it.
items.core_idea: Beauty is everywhere, poured out for you

items.plain: I must die, but must I die complaining? I must be chained, but must I also lament? I must go into exile, but can anyone stop me going with smiles, cheer and contentment?
items.core_idea: No one can force you to meet fate lamenting

items.plain: Since I'm naturally slow, should I not bother trying? Of course not. I'll never be the strongest or richest man, yet I still care for my body and property; we don't neglect anything just because we can't reach the top.
items.core_idea: Don't neglect effort because you can't be the best

items.plain: You call yourself a poor wretch with a miserable bit of flesh. Wretched, yes, but you have something better than your flesh. Why neglect the better part and cling to this?
items.core_idea: You have something better than your body

items.plain: Haven't you been given greatness of soul, courage and endurance? If I have greatness of soul, why worry about anything that might happen? What could disturb me? Shall I not use these powers as intended, instead of grieving over events?
items.core_idea: Use your inner powers instead of lamenting

items.plain: You won't endure and you're discontent: alone, you call it loneliness; with people, you call them crooks; you blame family and neighbours. Instead, call solitude peace and freedom, like the gods, and call company a festival, and accept everything contentedly.
items.core_idea: Rename your situation and accept it contentedly

items.plain: Epictetus said nothing great happens suddenly, not even a grape or a fig. A fig must flower, fruit, then ripen. If a fig takes time, how could you expect the fruit of a person's mind to come quickly and easily?
items.core_idea: Nothing great is produced suddenly

items.plain: Why do we get angry? Because we value so much what people take from us. Don't prize your clothes, and you won't be angry at the thief.
items.core_idea: Value things less and anger fades

items.plain: When a thief stole the iron lamp beside my household gods, I reflected that he had done nothing strange. Tomorrow I'll have a clay lamp instead; you can only lose what you have.
items.core_idea: We can only lose what we have

items.plain: When your head or ear hurts, don't cry 'alas'. You may groan aloud, but don't groan inwardly. If help is slow, don't torment yourself saying everyone hates you; who wouldn't dislike someone who behaves like that?
items.core_idea: Bear pain without inner complaint or self-pity

items.plain: What is free by nature can't be disturbed or hindered by anything except itself. It is a person's own opinions that disturb him.
items.core_idea: Our own opinions are what disturb us

items.plain: Difficulties show what people are. When one comes, remember God, like a wrestling trainer, has matched you with a tough opponent so you can become a champion, which takes sweat. No difficulty is more useful, if you use it.
items.core_idea: Difficulties are God's training for your strength

items.plain: Keep what is yours and don't crave what is others'. Your integrity and sense of shame are your own; who but you can take them or stop you using them? Yet chasing what isn't yours, you lose what is.
items.core_idea: Chasing others' things costs you your own

items.plain: Prizing my body or possessions makes me a slave, showing where I can be caught. Like a snake guarding its head, whatever you guard is where your master will strike. Knowing this, whom will you flatter or fear?
items.core_idea: What you cling to becomes your weak point

items.plain: It is we, or rather our opinions, that squeeze and trap us. What does insulting a stone achieve? If a person listens like a stone, the insulter gains nothing; he only succeeds by using the weakness of the one insulted.
items.core_idea: Insults only work through our own weakness

items.plain: Show me a place death never visits, or a charm against it. If there is none, what then? I can't escape death, but can't I escape fearing it, rather than die lamenting and trembling?
items.core_idea: You can't escape death, but you can escape fearing it

items.plain: God has set this law: if you want anything good, get it from yourself. You insist on getting it from someone else. Don't; get it from yourself.
items.core_idea: All good must come from yourself

items.plain: Freedom is simply the power to live as we choose. No one wants to live in error, fear, sorrow or turmoil, so no one living that way is free; whoever is rid of them is rid of slavery too.
items.core_idea: Freedom means release from fear and sorrow

items.plain: Things themselves don't matter, but how we use them does. To stay calm yet careful, act like a dice player: the dice and counters don't matter and I can't know the throw, but using the throw skilfully is my job.
items.core_idea: You can't control the throw, only its use

items.plain: Treat life like a voyage: I choose the captain, crew and day. In a storm, my part is done; the rest is the captain's. If the ship sinks, I won't drown fearful or blame God; I pass like an hour.
items.core_idea: Do your part, then accept what follows
items.extended_text: But we should act as we do in the case of a voyage. What can I do? I can choose the master of the ship, the sailors, the day, the opportunity. Then comes a storm. What more have I to care for? for my part is done. The business belongs to another, the master. But the ship is sinking--what then have I to do? I do the only thing that I can, not to be drowned full of fear, nor screaming nor blaming God, but knowing that what has been produced must also perish: for I am not an immortal being, but a man, a part of the whole, as an hour is a part of the day: I must be present like the hour, and past like the hour.

items.plain: Always remember what is yours and what belongs to someone else, and nothing will disturb you.
items.core_idea: Know what is yours and stay undisturbed

items.plain: You are something higher: a fragment of God, carrying a portion of him within you. Why then are you unaware of your noble origin? Why don't you know where you came from?
items.core_idea: You carry a portion of God within

items.plain: Each skill is kept up by practising it, and ruined by its opposite. Likewise modest, faithful acts preserve the modest and faithful person, while shameless, faithless, abusive, angry or greedy acts strengthen those very traits.
items.core_idea: What we repeatedly do shapes our character

items.plain: Storing bread and wine is different from eating them. What is eaten becomes muscle, flesh, blood and health. What is merely stored can be shown off when you like, but its only benefit is looking as if you have it.
items.core_idea: Knowledge must be digested, not just stored

items.plain: As a brother, give way, be easily persuaded, speak well of him, never fight him over things outside your will, and so gain more of what is within it. Trading a lettuce or seat for good character is a bargain.
items.core_idea: Yield outward things to gain good character

items.plain: Shall I not hurt someone who hurt me? First consider what hurt is. If good and evil lie in our will, then you are saying: since he harmed himself by wronging me, shall I harm myself by wronging him?
items.core_idea: Revenge only harms yourself

items.plain: When someone is anxious, ask what he wants; only wanting what's beyond his control makes him anxious. A lute player alone is calm, but in the theatre he is anxious, because he wants applause, which isn't in his power.
items.core_idea: Anxiety comes from wanting what we can't control

items.plain: Socrates' first and chief trait was never to get irritated in argument or say anything abusive or insulting, but to bear with abusive people and end the quarrel.
items.core_idea: Never be provoked; end the quarrel

items.plain: A guide who finds someone lost leads him to the right road; he doesn't mock him and walk off. Show the ignorant person the truth and he will follow. Until you can, don't ridicule him; recognise your own inability instead.
items.core_idea: Guide the mistaken; don't mock them

items.plain: What do we admire and busy ourselves with? External things. So why wonder that we are afraid and anxious? When we think what's coming is bad, we cannot help being fearful and anxious.
items.core_idea: Valuing externals breeds fear and anxiety

items.plain: The divine law: keep to your own, don't claim others' things, use what is given, don't crave what isn't, give back readily what is taken, and be thankful for the time you had it, rather than cry like a child.
items.core_idea: Use what is given; release it with thanks

items.plain: You long to see Athens and the Acropolis again? Aren't you content with what you see every day: sun, moon, stars, earth and sea? If you understand Him who governs everything and carry him within, why crave pretty stones?
items.core_idea: The daily world is wonder enough

items.plain: Every habit grows by matching actions: walking by walking, reading by reading. Stop for a month, or lie in bed ten days, and you feel the weakening. To build a habit, do it; to break one, do something else instead.
items.core_idea: Habits grow by doing and fade by stopping

items.plain: If you don't want to be quick-tempered, don't feed the habit. Stay calm and count the days without anger: every day, then every second, third, fourth. After thirty days, give thanks to God. The habit weakens, then disappears.
items.core_idea: Starve anger and count the calm days

items.plain: Don't be swept away by a sudden impression; tell it to wait while you test it. Don't let it paint vivid pictures of what follows; replace it with a noble impression. Practise this and you'll find real strength.
items.core_idea: Test impressions before letting them carry you

items.plain: The struggle is great and the work divine: it is for self-mastery, freedom, happiness and calm. Call on God for help, as sailors pray in a storm; no storm is worse than violent impressions that drive out reason.
items.core_idea: Call on God against storms of impression

items.plain: Friendship exists only where there is faithfulness, modesty and a sharing of honest things, and nothing else.
items.core_idea: Friendship rests on fidelity and honesty

items.plain: People act like a traveller heading home who stops at a pleasant inn and stays there. You've forgotten your purpose: you were passing through, not travelling to it. Many inns and meadows are pleasant, but only to pass through.
items.core_idea: Don't mistake a pleasant stop for the goal

items.plain: Thank God for sight, hearing, life itself and what sustains it, food, wine and oil. But remember he has given you something better than all these: the power to use them, test them and judge the worth of each.
items.core_idea: The power to judge things is God's best gift

items.plain: What are weeping and lamenting, bad luck, strife, blame and accusation? Opinions, nothing more: opinions that treat things outside our will as if they were good or bad.
items.core_idea: Our troubles are opinions about externals

items.plain: Your ship is lost; that is what happened. A man was taken to prison; that is what happened. That it went badly for him is something each person adds from his own opinion.
items.core_idea: Events are neutral; we add the misfortune

items.plain: Before you sleep, review each of the day's actions: what went wrong, what you did, what you left undone. Go through all of it, then blame what was wrong and rejoice in what was right.
items.core_idea: Review your day before sleeping

items.plain: Now it's time for fever, thirst or hunger: bear each well. Isn't that in your power? A doctor can stop you drinking or eating, but no one can stop you bearing thirst and hunger well.
items.core_idea: No one can stop you bearing hardship well

items.plain: My brother shouldn't have treated me like this. True, but that's his concern; however he behaves, I will act toward him as I should. My conduct is my business and no one can prevent it; his can be hindered.
items.core_idea: Others' conduct is theirs; yours is yours

items.plain: Loneliness is the state of feeling helpless. Being alone doesn't make you lonely, and being among many doesn't prevent it. When we lose a brother, son or friend we leaned on, we feel left alone even in a crowded city.
items.core_idea: Loneliness is helplessness, not being alone

items.plain: Still, a person should be ready for being alone too, able to be enough for himself and to be his own companion.
items.core_idea: Learn to be your own companion

items.plain: Like bad actors who can only sing in a chorus, some people can't walk alone. If you're anything, walk alone and talk to yourself; don't hide in the crowd. Look around, rouse yourself, and find out who you are.
items.core_idea: Step out of the crowd and know yourself

items.plain: Before any act, consider what comes before and after it, then proceed. If you don't, you'll start eagerly without thinking ahead, and when the consequences appear you'll give up shamefully.
items.core_idea: Consider the consequences before you begin

items.plain: If you often socialise with others, you will either become like them or change them. Put a dead coal beside a burning one: either the dead one puts out the other, or the live one lights it.
items.core_idea: Company either shapes you or is shaped by you

items.plain: My wife treats me badly, my father gives me nothing: that is all that happened. Calling it evil is a false addition. So rid yourself not of poverty but of your opinion of it, and you will be happy.
items.core_idea: Drop the opinion, not the hardship

items.plain: Who can force you to agree with what seems false? No one. Who can force you to deny what seems true? No one. So you can see there is something in you that is free by nature.
items.core_idea: Your judgement is naturally free

items.plain: Don't let what goes against nature in someone else become an evil for you. You were made by nature not to be downcast or unhappy along with others, but to be happy with them.
items.core_idea: Others' wrongs need not make you unhappy
